Package com.robojacks.lib.hardware

Class VexGps

java.lang.Object
com.robojacks.lib.hardware.VexGps
public class VexGps extends Object
V5 GPS Sensor: reads the field-perimeter code strip with a camera and reports where it is. Used like a PhotonVision camera: tell it where it's mounted with a robot-to-sensor transform, and getPose() returns the robot's pose on the field.

Mounting: robot-to-GPS transform

Same convention as WPILib and PhotonVision's robotToCamera: measured from the robot's center, in the robot's coordinate system
  • +X forward (toward the robot's front),
  • +Y left,
  • rotation counter-clockwise positive, viewed from above: the direction the GPS camera faces relative to the robot's front (0 = facing forward, 180 = facing backward, 90 = facing the robot's left side, -90 = its right side).

 // GPS 10 cm behind center and 5 cm right of it, camera facing out the back
 Transform2d kRobotToGps = new Transform2d(
         new Translation2d(-0.10, -0.05), Rotation2d.fromDegrees(180));
 VexGps m_gps = new VexGps(kGpsPort, kRobotToGps);

 Pose2d robotPose = m_gps.getPose();        // the robot's center, field frame
 Pose2d sensorPose = m_gps.getSensorPose(); // where the sensor itself is

Field frame: meters from the field center, heading counter-clockwise from +X (see the Units & field coordinates guide). Feed poses to a PoseEstimator through a GpsPoseEstimator to correct odometry.

The GPS can't see the strip when it's blocked or too close to the wall; getError() goes up when that happens.

    • setFieldHeadingOffset

      public void setFieldHeadingOffset(double degrees)
      Converts the GPS's compass heading into the field frame: field degrees = offset - GPS degrees. This is about which field wall is +X, not about mounting (that's setRobotToGps(com.robojacks.lib.math.Transform2d)). The default, 90, is right when the GPS's 0 points at the field's +Y wall. Check it once on a real field: with a forward-facing GPS, point the robot along +X and adjust until getRotation2d() reads 0.
